body:
## Why
npm is restricting 2FA-bypass tokens (direct publishing restricted Jan 2027) and its UI now says outright: "For automation or CI/CD uses, please use Trusted Publishing instead." Our v0.1.0 bootstrap used a 30-day bypass token because trusted publishers are configured in a package's settings page, which does not exist before first publish. The moment `hkb` exists on the registry, the token has no reason to live.

## What (after v0.1.0 is on the registry)
- On npmjs.com → package `hkb` → Settings → Trusted Publisher: GitHub Actions, org `emyann`, repo `harness-kanban-board`, workflow `release.yml`, allowed action `npm publish`.
- `release.yml`: ensure Node >= 22.14 and npm CLI >= 11.5.1 on the runner (docs requirement); keep `id-token: write`; REMOVE the `NODE_AUTH_TOKEN`/`NPM_TOKEN` wiring — with a trusted publisher, provenance and auth are automatic and no secret is read.
- Delete the `NPM_TOKEN` repo secret and revoke the npm token; update `docs/releasing.md` so the operator's only step is pushing the tag.
- Keep the graceful-degrade notice for forks (they have no trusted-publisher identity).

## Done when
A `v0.1.1` tag publishes with provenance and zero npm secrets in the repo, and the bypass token is revoked.
title: Switch the release to npm Trusted Publishing and delete NPM_TOKEN
